question: A 70-year-old man with Stage II colorectal cancer is assessed before treatment planning. He is confined to bed more than 50% of the day, requires assistance with self-care, and cannot perform work activities. What is his ECOG Performance Status score?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ECOG PS 1 = restricted in physically strenuous activity but able to carry out light work and ambulatory. This patient is far more limited.
ECOG PS 2 = ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to carry out any work activities; up and about more than 50% of waking hours. This patient is confined to bed >50% of the day.

Correct. ECOG PS 3 = limited self-care ability; confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours. This markedly impairs eligibility for curative-intent chemotherapy regimens and influences the risk-benefit discussion.
ECOG PS 4 = completely disabled; cannot carry out any self-care; totally confined to bed or chair. This patient retains some self-care ability.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the ECOG scale. Confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours with limited but not absent self-care = ECOG PS 3. This is a critical threshold affecting both curative eligibility and chemotherapy dosing.
Correct. ECOG PS 3 = confined to bed >50% of waking hours with limited self-care. Performance status is a critical determinant of treatment intent and regimen tolerability.
